extracted.intended_audience: general readers and film-interested audience seeking encyclopedic information about the film Vice (2018)
extracted.subtask_description: An encyclopedic Wikipedia entry summarizing the 2018 biographical black comedy film Vice: plot, cast, production, release, critical reception, historical accuracy issues, and awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performances / Acting
rubrics_metrics.description: "While the performances were universally acclaimed..." The performances of Christian Bale, Amy Adams and Sam Rockwell received critical acclaim, earning them Academy Award nominations (with Bale winning the Golden Globe).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article emphasizes transformative and lauded acting as a key positive: Bale's physical transformation (gaining 40 pounds) and critics' praise are cited. Examples: critics singled out Bale, Adams and Rockwell for awards consideration; Todd McCarthy praised the cast as rising to their challenges. Strong, transformative performances are treated as central to the film's merits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Screenplay and Direction
rubrics_metrics.description: McKay's screenplay and direction received both "scathing critiques and celebratory praise"; reviewers described the film as "messy but ambitious" and said the satire "tries too hard" in places.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation focuses on how well the writing and direction balance tone, structure, and argument. Critics' quoted opinions (e.g., IndieWire calling it 'messy but ambitious', Time calling it 'exhausting') illustrate that screenplay/direction are major axes of praise or criticism. Weaknesses cited include unfocused narrative and overreaching satire.

rubrics_metrics.name: Satirical Effectiveness / Political Satire
rubrics_metrics.description: The film is described as a biographical black comedy with "political satire elements"; critics note it 'provokes great laughs and hits home with some tragic truths' while others call it a 'cartoon villain' depiction or a 'witch hunt'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessments weigh whether the satire successfully balances humor and critique without reducing real events/people to caricature. Positive notes highlight moments that land 'satisfying bullseyes'; negative notes flag oversimplification or cartoonish portrayals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Historical Accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: "Numerous scenes from the film were identified as being historically inaccurate, heavily dramatized, or presented without necessary context." Politifact warned the 'line between historic facts and poetic interpretation gets fuzzy.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article lists concrete inaccuracies (fictionalized conversations, misrepresentations of the 'unitary executive' theory, altered chronology). For biopics, fidelity to historical record or clear signaling of dramatization is a key evaluative criterion; fact-checking sources (Politifact, HistoryvsHollywood, USA Today) are used to judge accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Makeup, Hairstyling and Physical Transformation
rubrics_metrics.description: Christian Bale gained 40 pounds for the role; make-up artistry by Greg Cannom was praised. The film won the Academy Award for Best Makeup and Hairstyling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Physical transformation and prosthetics/makeup are highlighted as measurable production achievements. Praise and awards in this category signal excellence; transformative actor preparation (weight changes) is also noted as contributing to performance credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Box Office Performance and Profitability
rubrics_metrics.description: The film grossed $76.1 million worldwide against a $60 million production budget and was 'considered a box office flop'; Variety later reported the film had never turned a profit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Box-office receipts, opening-weekend performance, territory breakdowns, and later reporting on profitability are used to evaluate commercial success. Comparisons to budget and contemporaneous releases (e.g., opening alongside Holmes & Watson) are part of the assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Critical Reception Metrics (Aggregators & Surveys)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rotten Tomatoes: 64% approval (average rating 6.7/10). Metacritic: 61/100. CinemaScore: average grade 'C+'. PostTrak: 72% overall positive, 49% 'definite recommend'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aggregator scores and audience surveys are presented as quantitative indicators of critical and viewer response. The article uses these metrics to summarize consensus and divergence among critics and audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure and Pacing / Narrative Coherence
rubrics_metrics.description: Critics criticized story pacing and structure: the film is described as 'a mess, zigging here and zagging there, never knowing quite when to end,' and 'exhausting.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Narrative coherence, pacing, and structural clarity are highlighted as aspects that affect critics' ability to engage with the film's themes. Negative commentary ties poor pacing/structure to diminished impact despite strong performances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Awards and Nominations
rubrics_metrics.description: The film received numerous accolades: eight Academy Award nominations (winning Best Makeup and Hairstyling), six Golden Globe and BAFTA nominations, Critics' Choice and other awards and nominations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Awards recognition (nominations and wins across major institutions) is used as an evaluative signal of industry and peer recognition, often cited alongside critical and commercial reception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Polarization / Divisiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: The film 'polarized critics; some considered it to be one of the best films of the year while others thought it to be one of the worst,' and it became 'one of the worst-reviewed films to ever be nominated for Best Picture.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Degree of divisiveness itself is treated as notable: a work that sharply splits opinion may be described as provocative or flawed depending on perspective. The article records both extremes to convey this polarization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Narrative Devices (Narrator, Fourth Wall, Nonlinear Elements)
rubrics_metrics.description: The film is narrated by a fictional character, includes a false epilogue, non-linear scenes, and a final breaking of the fourth wall where Cheney delivers a monologue to the audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Self-reflexive devices and unconventional narrative choices are noted as stylistic elements that shape reception; critics respond to whether such devices illuminate the subject or contribute to a sense of disjointedness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Portrayal of Real People: Responses from Subjects and Families
rubrics_metrics.description: Responses from the Cheney family are recorded: Liz Cheney criticized Christian Bale's portrayal and his Golden Globe acceptance remarks. The article documents public reactions from the family.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: How subjects and their families respond to portrayals is presented as an informative factor for evaluating fairness, accuracy, and reputational impact of a biopic. Negative reactions are cited as part of the film's reception narrative.
